title: The third law and rocket propulsion
canonical_question: How does Newton’s third law explain how a rocket accelerates?
summary: A rocket burns fuel and hurls hot gas out of its nozzle at high speed.
Because the interaction is between the rocket and its own exhaust, it works in the vacuum of space.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Push the gas, get pushed back
sections.body_md: A rocket burns fuel and hurls hot gas out of its nozzle at high speed. By the third law, as the rocket pushes the gas backward the gas pushes the rocket forward with an equal force. That forward reaction is the thrust.

sections.heading: No air required
sections.body_md: Because the interaction is between the rocket and its own exhaust, it works in the vacuum of space. The rocket does not push against the air or the ground. This is why rockets, unlike propellers, function beyond the atmosphere.

key_points: Rocket pushes exhaust back; exhaust pushes rocket forward.
The forward reaction is the thrust.
It needs no air to push against.
core.bridge_to_parent: It is a third-law application to propulsion.
